hooks.text: A cosmic giant crowned the biggest star in the universe suddenly shrank.
A massive star shrank from seventeen hundred solar radii down to nine hundred.
The largest known star in the universe lost its crown when astronomers remeasured its distance.

title: The Star That Shrank
description: Discover how the largest known star in the universe shrank by nearly half when astronomers remeasured its true distance.

beats.text: A cosmic giant crowned the biggest star in the universe suddenly shrank.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of red supergiant star UY Scuti compared to the Sun, 2012

beats.text: Back in 1860, astronomers at the Bonn Observatory cataloged a faint star in the constellation Scutum.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Bonn Observatory historic building, Germany

beats.text: Originally designated as BD-12 degrees 5055, its flickering brightness revealed a pulsating variable star.
beats.visual: Stellar light curve diagram showing variable star pulsation, 2015

beats.text: In 2012, Very Large Telescope interferometry in Chile calculated a staggering radius of 1,708 solar radii.
beats.visual: Very Large Telescope Cerro Paranal laser guide star in Atacama Desert Chile, 2012

beats.text: This massive size crowned UY Scuti the largest known star, with a volume swallowing Jupiter's orbit.
beats.visual: Solar system planets orbit diagram showing Jupiter orbit scale, 2020

beats.text: However, newer Gaia space telescope data revised its distance closer to Earth.
beats.visual: Gaia spacecraft model ESA artist concept in space, 2013

beats.text: The updated measurements shrank its official radius down to approximately 909 solar radii.
beats.visual: Artist concept of red supergiant star scaled down, 2021
